business: The Aldera, magnesium bisglycinate in daily sachets
why_not: I already take Toplux and reorder it when it runs out, so I have no reason to switch. $29.99 is more than what I pay now, and with two kids I am not paying extra for a pocket sachet when my gym bag already holds a bottle.
I already have my gummies that I reorder when they run out, and I'm not looking to switch. Two capsules every day is not something I want to swallow when I have something I like.
I don't take supplements unless a doctor tells me to, and nobody has told me I'm low on magnesium. Two capsules a day for $30 a month is money for something I don't think I need.
I already take magnesium at night at home, and I have a drawer of half-used bottles. I don't need one that fits in a gym bag.

I like the glycinate form and the batch QR report, but it's a brand I've never heard of with no reviews yet, and I read every review before I buy. At $29.99 it's more than Toplux or Goli, so I'd scroll past and maybe save it.

The dose and the bisglycinate form are right, and a batch report behind a QR code is more than most brands give. But it is a new brand with zero reviews, and I read every review before I buy, so I would not put money in on a TikTok video alone.

I'm a deal hunter and I already have a drawer of half-used supplement bottles. $24 for the first box is fine on paper, but I'd rather wait for a bigger coupon or a flash sale than pay full price for a brand I've never heard of.

A foil sachet for every single day is 30 pieces of trash a month, and I already know a bottle of magnesium glycinate costs less per day. 20% off is nice but I'd wait for a bigger coupon or a bundle anyway.
I'd scroll past. One form of magnesium in a sachet doesn't tell me why it's better than the multi-form capsules I can already get for less, and nothing here hits a problem I actually have right now.
why_yes: I forget my vitamins at home all the time and I live out of a gym bag, so a sachet I can toss in a pocket actually fits how I live. At $24 after the launch discount I would try one box, but only because of the sachet.

My doctor said my magnesium could be low and I always forget pills at home, so a sachet I can toss in my bag is the first version of this I would actually take. $24 with the launch discount is fine to try one box.

The batch-tested QR report and 200 mg bisglycinate with no oxide are what I look for, and with 20% off the first box it comes to about $24, close to what I already pay. The sachet is handy on work trips and for the gym bag, so I would try one box.
My doctor said my magnesium could be low, so this is a real problem and not just a cute video. With 20% off it comes to about $24, which I can stretch for one box, but I'd only try one and see.
